trust_decision.summary: Each media adapter's Next.js handler decides which bucket/container key an authorized editor may presign, write, delete or list. At the pinned commit it takes the caller-supplied key or directory as-is, with no traversal check and no confinement to the operator's mediaRoot.

landing_point.why: The advisory title names next-tinacms-s3 and 'arbitrary bucket-key write'. The presigned-upload GET branch is the S3 write primitive, and it passes req.query.key straight to getSignedUrl.

fix_sites.entry_point: DELETE /api/dos/media/[...key] (deleteAsset, split segments joined; mediaRoot newly passed at :72)

fix_sites.module_kind: second implementation (Azure Blob, app router, no mediaRoot concept)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: packages/next-tinacms-azure/src/handlers.ts:62 and packages/next-tinacms-cloudinary/src/handlers.ts:195-197 (sibling adapter packages with no mediaRoot option). The closest twin is packages/next-tinacms-dos/src/handlers.ts:117-121.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Azure and Cloudinary have no mediaRoot option (the fix itself says so at fix.diff:61-62 and fix.diff:307-308), so a solver can argue there is no boundary to escape there and that an authorized editor already owns the whole container. The listing routes can likewise be dismissed as read-only.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Deleting an item from the list must keep working. The list mapper returns id = the full object key, already prefixed with mediaRoot, and the client sends that id to DELETE. A fix that always prepends mediaRoot (or rejects keys that already carry it) double-prefixes or breaks delete. Other legitimate behaviour: literal '%' in names must not be re-decoded, inner '..' that stays inside is collapsed rather than rejected, and DOS keys split across route segments must still resolve.
